overview: The Council approved a utility petition for internet infrastructure and addressed several public safety concerns, including lead water service lines and utility company accountability. They also held an extensive discussion regarding the restoration of public access television and the potential location for a new studio.

items.title: Public Hearing: Light Tower Fiber Networks Utility Petition
items.summary: Approved a petition for underground conduit work at 200 Rivers Edge Drive to provide internet service to a new commercial tenant. The council received assurances that traffic flow would be maintained and the roadway restored to city standards.

items.title: Committee of the Whole Report
items.summary: Accepted a report from the Committee of the Whole that cleared several dozen long-standing papers from various subcommittees.

items.title: Utility Accountability and Restoration Standards
items.summary: Requested that the administration provide a comprehensive list of utility-related excavations and tree pruning needs to ensure adherence to city restoration standards and hold companies accountable for shoddy work.

items.title: West Medford Safety and Infrastructure
items.summary: Approved requests for the purchase of crime watch signs in West Medford and the installation of a thermoplastic crosswalk at the corner of Grove Street and Buzzle Road.

items.title: Republic Parking Contract Review
items.summary: Requested that the City Solicitor review the city's contract with Republic Parking following the company's sale and provide a legal briefing on potential termination clauses.

items.title: SeeClickFix Policies and Distracted Driving Enforcement
items.summary: Requested operational guidelines for the SeeClickFix system to prevent it from being used as a public blog and called for increased police enforcement of distracted driving laws.

items.title: Lead Water Service Lines Awareness
items.summary: Requested that the Water Department notify residents of known lead service lines and identify potential MWRA funding sources to assist homeowners with the cost of replacement.

items.title: Brewster Road Construction Notification
items.summary: Requested that the administration provide Brewster Road residents with a detailed timeline and city point of contact for an upcoming drainage project.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions and Local Events
items.summary: Congratulated the MHS Drama Club, Boy Scout Troop 416, and the Middle Schools String Ensemble on recent achievements, and recognized participants in the Boston Marathon and a local addiction awareness vigil.

items.title: MHS Band Trailer and Carr Park Repairs
items.summary: Requested a status update on a new band trailer for Medford High School and the immediate repair of exposed electrical ground boxes at Carr Park.

items.title: Restoration of Public Access Television (TV3)
items.summary: Discussed the long-delayed restoration of a public access station, resulting in a request for an update from the Mayor and a legal opinion on whether live-streaming city meetings constitutes copyright infringement. Residents argued against the proposed high school location in favor of a more centrally located studio in the library or Medford Square.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the April 12, 2016, meeting as amended to include specific athletic achievements.
